facts.fact: The World Bank and Government of Togo case study says NOVISSI's system automatically sent payroll files through an API to the two mobile network operators (Togocom and Moov Africa Togo), whose mobile money systems were made interoperable with it, and paid over 920,000 people by August 2021.

The case study says NOVISSI registrations were validated automatically against the voter list (unique voter number, NSF code, location, sex, occupation) and, for model 2, against a potential-eligibility list of phone numbers supplied by academics; the voter list stood in for a missing foundational ID.

The case study says Togo is building, under a US$72 million IDA-financed WURI programme, a foundational unique identification platform for all residents, to be the basis of a dynamic social registry of individuals and households, both listed as priorities of the 2020-2025 government roadmap.
facts.system: Foundational unique ID platform (WURI) and planned dynamic social registry

facts.fact: The case study says that during NOVISSI's operation (2020-2021) Togo had no dynamic social registry and no unique identifier covering all residents, so some households may have received multiple transfers because the assistance unit was the individual.
